messages.author: 06d3f312dd6c0698
messages.subject: difference of splines
parts:
Hi, 

is there a way to generate a model of the form 

y ~ s(x) + "s(x, by=fact)"

where the second term (for fac being a factor with two levels) is the difference of the smooth of these levels ? That is, if the levels are A and B, then I am interested in s(x):B - s(x):A

When fitting 

y ~ s(x, by=fact)

I have access to the smooths for each level, but I am also interested in credible intervals for the difference, and it is not obvious to me how I would extract it from this simple model

Best,
:)
pawel

messages.author: 6e3dd74b422c061b
messages.subject: Re: difference of splines
parts:
Hmm I haven't thought about such a question before.

It seems as if you main question refers to comparing the difference of the splines, that is the difference across a range of values of x, right (since the spline will likely be non-linear)?

You could try using fitted with newdata specifying the conditions (x values) you want to compare and summary = FALSE. Then, you could substract the relevant columns from each other and compute summary estimates.

messages.author: 6e3dd74b422c061b
messages.subject: Re: [brms-users] Re: difference of splines
parts:
No, you get both Estimates and CIs out of my approach.

When you compute the difference of the splines for fitted(..., summary = FALSE), you compute this difference of each posterior sample.
Then you can obtain CIs for instance via quantiles (using the quantile function).

Best,
Paul
